cases.name: useful-text-exploration-without-gui-tools
cases.trap: Missing GUI tools causes refusal or vague requirements prose instead of a concrete, bounded navigation experiment.
cases.prompt: I'm designing a TUI for a Kubernetes cluster manager. The user should view all pods, filter by namespace, select a pod, and view its logs in a split panel. We have no running terminal prototype today. Explore the navigation design inline before we build it, including what happens when a filter removes the selected pod.
expectations: Shows concrete terminal/state representations for the list, selected-pod log view, and filter interaction, with labeled regions and meaningful key bindings.
Walks the same user journey through those states, including focus and the log panel when the filter excludes the selected pod.
Identifies unresolved choices as questions or proposals, not observed behavior or accepted backend guarantees.
Uses the text experiment productively and states what actual terminal interaction would still need to establish.
negative_expectations: Do not refuse useful exploration merely because no GUI/terminal prototype tool is available.
Do not provide only a static layout or a restatement of the feature request.
Do not claim a terminal was rendered, users were observed, or focus was verified.

cases.name: migration-transcript-negative-paths
cases.trap: A happy-path transcript hides partial failure or invents transactional rollback to make the experience look complete.
cases.prompt: Create inline command-transcript prototypes for dbmigrate up, down, and status. Include no pending migrations, down with nothing applied, and an up run where the first migration succeeds and the second fails. The tool will also run in CI. Product policy has not yet fixed rollback semantics or whether callers need distinct failure codes. Make those design decisions visible without treating proposals as accepted guarantees.
expectations: Produces concrete illustrative invocations, output, and exit outcomes for success, both no-work cases, and a failure after one migration has succeeded.
Separates stdout data from stderr diagnostics and addresses non-interactive CI behavior.
Makes preserved progress, retry safety, and rollback uncertainty explicit rather than inventing a transaction guarantee.

Explains whether distinct exit codes serve a real caller decision. Either a shared nonzero failure code or separate codes is defensible with a clear proposed contract; no-work success is distinguished from actual failure.
States the questions/decisions the transcripts reveal and the limits of this unexecuted experiment.
negative_expectations: Do not omit the first-succeeded/second-failed case or describe only ideal success.
Do not claim commands ran or rollback/persistence was observed.
Do not mandate a unique exit code per error without a caller need or suppress failure under quiet/CI operation.

cases.name: prototype-to-handoff-with-a-real-gap
cases.trap: Visual satisfaction is mistaken for a resolved design, or a reviewer fabricates a gap instead of inspecting the supplied transition contract.
cases.prompt: Our username-field sketch has six states: empty, typing, validating, available, taken, error. Editing a value from any result state enters typing and clears the old result. A debounce enters validating; a response enters available/taken/error. Submit is disabled during validating and taken. The sketch does not define Submit behavior in error. No running prototype or backend submission contract is available. I like how it looks. Are we ready to hand this to implementation? Give the next action inline.
expectations: Identifies the supplied missing error-state Submit behavior as a consequential unresolved choice, without inventing unseen defects as facts.
Separates the human-facing choice from the unestablished backend validation guarantee.
Maps settled states/transitions and rationale into the existing design handoff while keeping the dependent gap explicitly unresolved.
Recommends further experimentation only for a named question it can answer; does not refine a prototype indefinitely.
negative_expectations: Do not declare implementation readiness from appearance alone or hand off an unresolved error path as settled.
Do not silently authorize submission, persistence, or backend validation.
Do not invent an exact required handoff heading or demand another prototype when a decision from the owner is what is missing.

cases.name: same-scenario-comparison-not-preselected-winner
cases.trap: Abstract pros and cons or a preferred pattern replace a comparable experiment; one approach receives an easier scenario than the other.
cases.prompt: For a TUI file manager, compare (A) a persistent filter bar above the file list and (B) a search surface opened with '/'. Users must find matching files, inspect one, and return; sometimes there are no matches or the user cancels mid-edit. The direction is genuinely open. Explore both inline and recommend a direction or the specific observation still needed to choose.
expectations: Runs the same concrete find/inspect/return scenario through both approaches and includes no-results or cancellation.
Makes focus, retained filter/selection, discoverability, and recovery trade-offs visible for each.
Identifies what each approach leaves uncertain rather than praising the favored option and omitting its costs.
Recommends either approach with scenario-grounded rationale, or names a consequential observation needed to decide. Does not require one preselected winner.
States what decisions and limits belong in the existing design handoff.
negative_expectations: Do not provide only generic pros/cons, color variations, or a popularity-based winner.
Do not claim real user preference or interaction evidence from an inline simulation.
Do not replace a concrete design decision with an unexplained 'it depends'.
